title: GST 111 (COOU) | Chapter Three: The Use of the Dictionary
subject: GST 111

questions.question: A dictionary is a reference book containing the words of a language usually arranged:
questions.explanation: A dictionary is a reference book containing the words of a language usually alphabetically arranged.

questions.question: According to Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary, a dictionary is a book that gives a list of the words of a language in:
questions.explanation: The dictionary gives a list of words of a language in alphabetical order and explains what they mean.

questions.question: Besides explaining meanings, the Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary states that a dictionary can give a word for them in a:
questions.explanation: A dictionary can give a word for them in a foreign language, e.g. a Spanish-English dictionary.

questions.question: A dictionary of mathematics is given as an example of a dictionary that explains words that are in a:
questions.explanation: A dictionary of mathematics explains the words that are in a particular subject.

questions.question: A dictionary can also be a list of words in electronic form, for example stored in a computer's:
questions.explanation: The Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary cites a list of words in electronic form stored in a computer's spellchecker.

questions.question: The Oxford English Dictionary defines a dictionary as a book dealing with the individual words of a language so as to set forth their orthography, pronunciation, signification and:
questions.explanation: The OED definition includes orthography, pronunciation, signification and use, among others.

questions.question: The word list of a dictionary may be general or restricted, covering regional and social dialects, jargons, slangs and:
questions.explanation: Criterion one concerns density of entries: whether the word list is general or restricted and whether it covers dialects, jargons, slangs and archaisms.

questions.question: Which criterion classifies dictionaries as monolingual, bilingual or multilingual?
questions.explanation: The number of languages involved determines whether a dictionary is monolingual, bilingual or multilingual.

questions.question: The axis of time criterion classifies dictionaries as diachronic or:
questions.explanation: Under axis of time, dictionaries are either diachronic (dynamic) or synchronic (static).

questions.question: Dictionaries may be classified according to the arrangement of entries as alphabetical, semantic or:
questions.explanation: Arrangement of entries may be alphabetical or semantic or causal.

questions.question: When classifying by purpose, dictionaries are described as normative or:
questions.explanation: Under purpose, dictionaries are described as normative or referential.

questions.question: The criterion that considers whether a dictionary is meant for the general reader or for special users is the:
questions.explanation: The prospective user criterion asks whether the dictionary is meant for the general reader or for special users.

questions.question: On the basis of the criteria of classification, the dictionary is broadly divided into linguistic dictionaries and:
questions.explanation: The dictionary is broadly divided into linguistic dictionaries and encyclopaedia dictionaries.

questions.question: Linguistic dictionaries deal with only the lexical stock, that is, words as:
questions.explanation: The linguistic dictionary deals with only the lexical stock, that is, words as speech material.

questions.question: Linguistic dictionaries may also be called a:
questions.explanation: Linguistic dictionaries may be called a 'word book'.

questions.question: When linguistic dictionaries are divided by the scope of their word list, they are classified as general and:
questions.explanation: According to the scope of their word list, linguistic dictionaries are divided into general and restricted.

questions.question: The terms general and restricted in dictionary classification do not refer to the:
questions.explanation: The terms general and restricted do not refer to the size of the dictionary or to the number of items listed.

questions.question: General dictionaries represent the vocabulary as a whole with a degree of completeness depending upon the scope and the:
questions.explanation: General dictionaries represent the vocabulary as a whole with completeness depending upon the scope and the bulk of the book.

questions.question: Frequency dictionaries inform the user as to the frequency of occurrence of lexical units in:
questions.explanation: Dictionaries of word frequency inform the user as to the frequency of occurrence of lexical units in speech.

questions.question: The academic dictionary gives the lexical stock of the standard language with the aim to present the language as it is expected to be and:
questions.explanation: The academic dictionary aims to present the language as it is expected to be and stop it from decay.

questions.question: The referential or descriptive dictionary does not have any:
questions.explanation: The referential or descriptive dictionary does not have any normative aim.

questions.question: The corpus of a referential dictionary includes not only literary texts but also:
questions.explanation: The corpus includes not only literary texts but also oral literature.

questions.question: Restricted dictionaries cover only a certain specific part of the:
questions.explanation: Restricted dictionaries cover only a certain specific part of the vocabulary.

questions.question: The first subgroup of restricted dictionaries registers and explains technical terms for various branches of:
questions.explanation: The first subgroup registers and explains technical terms for various branches of knowledge.

questions.question: Dictionaries recording the complete vocabulary of some author are called:
questions.explanation: Dictionaries recording the complete vocabulary of some author are called concordances.

questions.question: Dictionaries that deal only with difficult words are distinguished from concordances and are called:
questions.explanation: Those that deal only with difficult words are called glossaries.

questions.question: According to the information they provide, all linguistic dictionaries fall into two groups: explanatory and:
questions.explanation: All linguistic dictionaries fall into explanatory and specialized groups according to the information they provide.

questions.question: Explanatory dictionaries present a wide range of data, especially with regard to the semantic aspect of the:
questions.explanation: Explanatory dictionaries present data especially with regard to the semantic aspect of the vocabulary items entered.

questions.question: Specialized dictionaries deal with lexical units only in relation to some of their characteristics such as etymology, frequency, pronunciation and:
questions.explanation: Specialized dictionaries deal with lexical units in relation to etymology, frequency, pronunciation and usage.

questions.question: The world famous English Pronouncing Dictionary was compiled by:
questions.explanation: The English Pronouncing Dictionary by Daniel Jones provides the most expert guidance on English and American English pronunciation.

questions.question: Dictionaries of synonyms, antonyms and ideographical dictionaries are classified on the basis of their semantic aspect and their:
questions.explanation: These dictionaries are classified on the basis of their semantic aspect and their relational value in the lexical stock.

questions.question: According to the language of explanations, all dictionaries are divided into:
questions.explanation: According to the language of explanations, dictionaries are divided into monolingual and bilingual.

questions.question: In monolingual dictionaries, the words and the information about them are given in:
questions.explanation: In monolingual dictionaries, the words and information about them are given in the same language.

questions.question: Bilingual dictionaries explain words by giving their equivalents in:
questions.explanation: Bilingual dictionaries explain words by giving their equivalents in another language.

questions.question: The two principal purposes of bilingual dictionaries are reference for translation and:
questions.explanation: Bilingual dictionaries have two principal purposes: reference for translation and guidance for expression.

questions.question: Diachronic (historical) dictionaries record the history of form and meaning for every word:
questions.explanation: Diachronic dictionaries record the history of form and meaning for every word registered.

questions.question: The main example of a diachronic dictionary is:
questions.explanation: The Oxford English Dictionary is the main example of a diachronic dictionary.

questions.question: Synchronic or descriptive dictionaries are concerned with the present-day meaning and:
questions.explanation: Synchronic dictionaries are concerned with the present-day meaning and usage of words.

questions.question: In the ideographic dictionaries, the main body is arranged according to a logical classification of:
questions.explanation: In ideographic dictionaries the main body is arranged according to a logical classification of notions expressed.

questions.question: The Latin word thesaurus means:
questions.explanation: The Latin word thesaurus means 'treasury'.

questions.question: P. Roget's book gave the word thesaurus the new figurative meaning of a store of:
questions.explanation: P. Roget's book gave the word thesaurus the new figurative meaning of 'a store of knowledge'.

questions.question: The ideographic type of dictionary supplies the word or words by which a given idea may be:
questions.explanation: The thesaurus supplies the word or words by which a given idea may be expressed.

questions.question: Cultural literacy is a term coined by:
questions.explanation: Cultural literacy is a term coined by E. D. Hirsch.

questions.question: A culturally literate person knows a given culture's signs and:
questions.explanation: A culturally literate person knows a given culture's signs and symbols, including its language and idioms.

questions.question: Encyclopaedic information has the features of including names of persons, places and literary works, covering all branches of human knowledge and giving:
questions.explanation: The encyclopaedic information features extensive treatment of facts, among others.

questions.question: Most proper names will not occur in a dictionary but of course occur in an:
questions.explanation: Most proper names will not occur in a dictionary but of course occur in an encyclopaedia.

questions.question: The English spelling system is problematic for foreign learners because initials of certain words are not pronounced, as in:
questions.explanation: Initials of certain words are not pronounced, as in pneumonia, mnemonic, honest and psychology.

questions.question: Which pair of words is pronounced alike?
questions.explanation: Pairs such as piece and peace, stationery and stationary are pronounced alike.

questions.question: Which of these is a difference between British and American English spelling?
questions.explanation: British English 'colour' corresponds to American English 'color'.

questions.question: When you find a new word while reading, you should first finish the sentence or the:
questions.explanation: When you find a new word while reading, finish the sentence or the paragraph before looking it up.

questions.question: When you hear a new word in class, you should wait and continue:
questions.explanation: When you hear a new word in class, wait and continue listening as what the teacher says next may help you.
